claim: Forty participants, 20 young and 20 old, completed a training programme, and a performance score was recorded before and after it. Claim: the mean improvement (after minus before) is larger in young than in old participants, judged by a one-sided test of the difference between the two groups' mean improvements at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: performance score before the programme
performance score after the programme
True for young participants, False for old participants

claim: The daily predictors X carry information about the daily outcome y on future days: the Pearson correlation between y and the prediction of a ridge regression of y on X (penalty 1.0 on standardised predictors, with an intercept), computed over future days, is at least 0.20.

data_keys.meaning: 6 continuous daily predictor series, one value per predictor per day
continuous daily outcome

claim: Among 3 groups of 25 rats each, mean resting oxygen uptake differs between the groups once body mass is accounted for: the analysis-of-covariance F test of the group effect on oxygen uptake, with body mass as the covariate, has a p-value below 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: resting oxygen uptake of each rat in each group, in mL O2 per min
body mass of each rat in each group, in g

claim: In at least 60% of the species, femur length and humerus length are positively associated after accounting for body length: within the species, the partial correlation between femur length and humerus length, given body length, is at least 0.2.

data_keys.meaning: femur length of each individual sampled in each species, in mm
humerus length of each individual sampled in each species, in mm
head-and-body length of each individual sampled in each species, in mm

claim: Expression profiles together with clinical covariates predict tumour response in new patients: the Pearson correlation between predicted and observed response is at least 0.30.

data_keys.meaning: log2 expression level of each gene in each patient's tumour sample
standardised clinical covariates of each patient (age, tumour size, and similar)
percentage tumour shrinkage measured after treatment

claim: A nearest-neighbour classifier (one neighbour, Euclidean distance on standardised measurements) recovers the rare outcome y from the measurements X for new patients with a balanced accuracy (mean of sensitivity and specificity) of at least 0.65.

data_keys.meaning: 15 continuous clinical measurements for each patient
True where the patient has the rare outcome

claim: After accounting for body mass, kidney weight and heart weight are positively related: the standardised slope of kidney weight on heart weight is at least 0.25.

data_keys.meaning: combined kidney weight of each rat, in g
heart weight of each rat, in g
body mass of each rat, in g

claim: Across 25 populations of one beetle species, with 40 specimens measured in each, wing length rises with head width at a given body length: the mean over populations of the within-population multiple-regression coefficient of wing length on head width, with body length as the other predictor, is at least 0.30 (mm of wing length per mm of head width).

data_keys.meaning: head width of each specimen in each population, in mm
wing length of each specimen in each population, in mm
body length of each specimen in each population, in mm
